I'll invoke the alchemy skill as requested.

## What I found

This directory has no application code — only `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/skills/`. Nothing about "our web app" was verifiable: not the stack, not whether usage data is queryable, not whether email sending already exists, not what an "account owner" is in your model. So the design below is stated as mechanism-neutral structure plus explicitly named assumptions.

The decision: **build the smallest version of it — one scheduled job, one database table, one email template, one unsubscribe link (the record calls this `BUILD-minimal`)** — and do not build a notification framework. The fact that decided it: there is exactly one digest type, so an abstraction over "notification kinds" has no second instance (Rule of 3), and the only genuinely load-bearing complexity is a single uniqueness constraint that stops a retrying scheduler from mailing every customer twice.

Three things are product decisions, not design decisions, and they are unanswerable from here: **which numbers go in the email**, **what week boundary and timezone**, and **whether a zero-usage account gets an email at all**.

## Why it matters

Acting: you get a reversible weekly email whose blast radius is your entire paying customer base, which is why the idempotency key and the opt-out link are in the minimum and not in "phase 2." Not acting, or acting without the three answers above: the usual failure is not a bug but an email nobody opens — and with no engagement measure wired in, you won't be able to tell, so the thing survives on sentiment. Beyond that I can't reach: I have no evidence anyone asked for this email, so its value is a hypothesis, not a finding.

## Do this first

1. Answer the three open product questions (metric set, week/timezone, zero-usage policy) — defaults are proposed in the readiness record below; if you take the defaults, say so and the design is unblocked.
2. Check two facts in the real repo, which settle most remaining mechanism choices: `grep -ril "sendgrid\|postmark\|ses\|resend\|nodemailer\|mailer" <repo>` for an existing email adapter, and look for an existing scheduled-job entry point (cron, Celery beat, `schedule.yaml`, platform cron).
3. Write the dependency rules for the new subsystem before its code, in the same PR (`architecture-as-code` §6).

## The design

```text
platform scheduler (weekly, one timezone)
  └─ digest-job.run(periodStart, periodEnd)            ← orchestration, I/O
       for each eligible owner:                         ← one query: owner + email + not opted out
         claim: INSERT digest_send(account_id, period_start, 'pending')
                ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING                  ← the idempotency key
         not claimed → skip
         model  = summarize(usageRows, period)          ← pure, no I/O
         empty and policy=skip → mark 'skipped'
         msg    = render(model)                         ← pure, no I/O
         email-adapter.send(msg)                        ← existing provider, reused
         mark 'sent' | 'failed'

GET /digest/unsubscribe?t=<signed token>  → set opt_out, confirm page, no login
```

Four properties carry the whole design: `summarize` and `render` are pure (unit-testable without mocks); one row per `(account, week)` makes a double send unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely; one account's failure never aborts the run; and the unsubscribe link authenticates itself with a signed, purpose-scoped token rather than relying on URL obscurity.

What is deliberately absent: no channel abstraction, no template engine beyond what you have, no per-metric plugin registry, no retry queue, no second email provider client, no per-user send times.

---

## Stage records

**Requirements Grounding**

```text
Subject:        weekly usage summary to account owners
Mode:           conversational
Decision:       PROVISIONAL
Problem:        (inferred) An account owner cannot tell, without logging in, whether
                their account is getting value from the product week to week; nothing
                reaches them where they already are.
Basis profile:  hypothesized (need), interpreted (opt-out obligation)
Confidence:     low
Blocking gaps:  metric set; definition of "account owner"; zero-usage policy;
                no evidence any owner asked for this
Outcome hypotheses: digest-engagement (below)
Supersedes:     none
Next action:    confirm the three gaps with the product owner
Verification:   workspace inspection only — no app code, sources, or telemetry present
Revisit when:   first four weeks of sends are measured
```

Candidates:

```text
Requirement: weekly-usage-summary
Actor: account owner
Must be able to: receive, without logging in, a weekly account-usage summary
Complete when:
- an owner with usage in a completed week receives exactly one summary for it
- the summary's figures equal the figures the product reports for that period
Basis: hypothesized | Priority: must | Validation: test | Confidence: low

Requirement: summary-opt-out
Actor: account owner
Must be able to: stop receiving the summary in one action, without logging in
Complete when:
- the email carries a working opt-out link
- no further summary is sent after opt-out
Basis: interpreted (CAN-SPAM / ePrivacy practice — source not verified here)
Priority: must | Validation: accept | Confidence: medium

Requirement: at-most-one-per-week
Actor: account owner
Must be able to: rely on never receiving a duplicate summary for one week
Complete when:
- re-running the job for a period sends nothing further
Basis: interpreted (reliability sweep) | Priority: must | Validation: test | Confidence: high
```

Quality sweep: reliability `covered` by `at-most-one-per-week`; security/privacy `covered` by `summary-opt-out` plus the token decision in A (owner data must not reach a non-owner); functional suitability `open` — owner, product: the metric set; interaction capability `open` — plain-text alternative and accessible HTML, owner: whoever owns email templates; performance efficiency `not applicable` — a weekly batch at account scale; safety, compatibility, flexibility `not applicable` with reason.

```text
Outcome hypothesis: digest-engagement
Applies to requirements: weekly-usage-summary
If: owners receive the weekly summary
Then: a meaningful share open it and click through to the product
Primary measure: open rate and click-through rate per send cohort
Baseline: unknown | Decision threshold: to be set by the owner before the first send
Evaluation window: first 4 weekly sends
Guardrails: opt-out rate; spam-complaint rate
Evidence state: unmeasured
Revisit when: 4 sends complete
```

**M — Minimum**

```text
Subject:        weekly usage summary email
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Pass
Necessity note: A periodic push summary is not an impossible-state guard and no
                layer beneath owns it. Unverified risk: if an in-app usage
                dashboard already exists, this duplicates its content in a new
                channel and I drops from 2 to 1.
V scores:       U=1 nothing breaks without it; no request evidence
                F=2 the need is asserted weekly, not evidenced
                R=3 every account owner is in scope by definition
                I=2 alternative is "log in and look", assuming a dashboard exists
C scores:       Subsystem-kinds Δ=+1  Dependency-edges Δ=+4
                Max-chain-depth Δ=0..+1  Subsystem-count Δ=+1   (measured at C)
                M=2 template, fixtures, and a provider dependency to keep green
                X=2 wrong or duplicated mail reaches the entire customer base
                E=1 confined to its own subsystem
Confidence V:   Low
Confidence C:   Low-Medium
Outcome evidence: digest-engagement — unmeasured
Decision:       BUILD-minimal
Rationale:      Medium V against low C. The Low-V-confidence default of DEFER is
                overridden deliberately: the increment is small, removable, and
                explicitly requested, and the missing evidence is exactly what the
                first four sends produce. Recorded as an override, not a pass.
Next action:    build the slice below with engagement instrumentation in the same PR
Verification:   Not run — no code, telemetry, or ticket source available
Minimal alt:    three headline numbers plus a link to the dashboard, not a report
Revisit when:   after 4 sends — if click-through is below the owner's threshold or
                opt-out exceeds the guardrail, re-enter M in retrospective mode
```

**Implementation Readiness**

```text
Subject:            weekly-digest increment
Decision:           PARTLY-READY
Requirement IDs:    weekly-usage-summary, summary-opt-out, at-most-one-per-week
Prerequisites:      assumed — queryable per-account usage data, a transactional email
                    provider, a platform scheduler. None verified.
Blocking gaps:      metric set (product owner); recipient definition (product owner);
                    zero-usage policy (product owner)
Smallest increment: one scheduled run → eligible owners → 3 pure-computed figures →
                    one template → existing provider → one send-log row →
                    working unsubscribe
Open decisions:     product: the three gaps above.
                    ADR seeds: (1) week boundary and timezone — default UTC,
                    Mon 00:00–Sun 23:59, send Monday morning, because per-owner
                    timezones multiply runs and complicate the idempotency key;
                    (2) unsubscribe token — signed, purpose-scoped, no session;
                    (3) zero-usage — default skip the send.
Next action:        confirm or accept the three defaults, then build
Verification:       readiness checklist against the grounding record; no artifacts to inspect
Revisit when:       any default is rejected
```

Parallel-ready: no — single increment. The three open decisions change the email's content and schedule, not its structure or its verification, which is what makes this partly ready rather than not ready.

**Test Strategy — Obligation pass**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `weekly-usage-summary` | Figures disagree with the product | Same source query as the in-app view, fixed fixtures | Examples + boundary (week edges, timezone) |

| `summary-opt-out` | Opted-out owner still receives it | Recipient set excludes opt-outs | Decision table |

**Evolutionary Database Design — Combined pass**

| Element | Class | Writer / readers | Mode | Stage | Reversal | Blind spot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `digest_send(account_id, period_start, status, sent_at)`, unique on `(account_id, period_start)` | Additive (new table) | digest-job / digest-job only | full | single step | drop table | none |
| owner `digest_opt_out bool not null default false` | Additive (defaulted column) | digest-job + unsubscribe route / digest-job | full | single step | drop column | an unknown reader of the owner table that enumerates columns |
| existing usage data | unchanged | — / **digest-job is a new reader** | — | — | — | future changes to this shape now break the digest |

```text
Decision:             COMPATIBLE
Change class:         additive
Compatibility mode:   full — old code ignores the new table and column
Coexistence window:   any rollout plus its rollback target
Reversibility input:  reversible data change
Staged path:          single step; no expand/contract, no backfill (the default covers existing rows)
Data contract:        digest_send is private to the digest subsystem — no external consumer
Obligations:          opt-out state must survive; do not purge it with send history
Handoffs:             test-strategy (migration runs against a production-shaped DB), shift-left (8a dry-run)
Residual risk:        the digest silently becomes a second reader of the usage shape
Next action:          record the digest as a consumer wherever usage-shape changes are reviewed
Verification:         Not run — no schema or migration tool present
```

**A — Architecture**

```text
Subject:        weekly-digest subsystem
Decision:       Proceed
Principle:      functional core (pure summarize/render, I/O at the edges); SRP
                (one reason to change: the weekly digest); YAGNI + Rule of 3
                (no channel/notification abstraction — no second instance exists);
                idempotency (claim-before-send); failure classification (per-owner
                send is best-effort and isolated; usage-store unavailability is hard);
                atomicity (partial success accepted, per §7c, decided now);
                layer self-sufficiency (unsubscribe and any HTTP job trigger
                authorize on their own — not via URL obscurity or network placement);
                integration (reuse the existing provider adapter; do not add a
                second SDK client)
Evidence:       no repository artifacts — principles applied to the proposed design
Enforcement:    add architecture rule: forbid digest-core -> * except digest-core
                add architecture rule: forbid * -> digest-internal-* except digest-*
                add architecture rule: forbid * -> <email provider SDK> except <email adapter>
                none — layer self-sufficiency is not an import edge; verify by
                exercising unsubscribe with no network restriction (shift-left)
Next action:    write the rule file, then the code
Verification:   Not run — no code to lint
```

Complexity Warning: a generic notification/subscription framework introduces new subsystem kinds, roughly ten dependency edges, and two extra chain hops to serve one digest type. The simpler alternative is the single job above; revisit only when a *second* recurring email is actually named.

**L — Locality (Rapid)**

```text
Subject:             weekly-digest
Mode:                Design
Analysis mode:       Rapid
Selection reason:    one bounded placement with a handful of proposed static edges
Decision:            PLACE
Declared topology:   <account-engagement domain> / capability tier / application layer
                     inbound: digest-job.run(period) + unsubscribe route handler
                     outbound: usage read interface, owner read interface,
                     email adapter, digest_send store
Position legality:   Not evaluated — no declared topology artifact exists in this
                     workspace, so neither endpoint of any edge has a position.
                     This is placement ambiguity from missing inputs, not from an
                     incoherent design; resolve by mapping onto the repo's real
                     domain paths before merge.
Observed fields:     Not measured — Rapid inspects declared/proposed static edges only
Static cycle:        Pass — nothing depends on the digest; the digest depends only
                     on existing inbound interfaces
Runtime cycles:      none
Boundary evidence:   domain reason only (its own name, lifecycle, and reason to
                     change); no independent field, and none required for PLACE
Enforcement:         add architecture rule: forbid digest-* -> <usage internals>,
                     except via the usage domain's inbound interface
Next action:         if an email/notifications subsystem already exists, attach the
                     digest to it as a caller rather than owning a provider adapter
Verification:        Not run — no import graph available
```

**C — Complexity**

```text
Subject:              one digest subsystem vs. (a) a notification framework, (b) no send-log table
Decision:             Proceed
Subsystem-kinds Δ:    +1  (a scheduled-batch-job kind, if the app has none yet; 0 if it does)
Dependency-edges Δ:   +4  (digest → usage read, owner read, email adapter, digest_send)
Max-chain-depth Δ:    0..+1 (scheduler → job → core; unlikely to exceed the app's longest chain)
Subsystem-count Δ:    +1  (one subsystem; plus one table, one route, one job entry)
Cycle:                Pass
Non-structural gates: Pass — behavior, privacy (opt-out, owner-scoped token),
                      observability (below), migration and rollback all hold
Trade-off:            §6 "add abstraction tier — <3 instances or speculative" rejects
                      the framework; §7c atomicity accepts the send-log table's cost
Rationale:            Alternative (a) raises all four axes to serve one digest type and
                      cannot name a second instance — rejected. Alternative (b) saves
                      one table and one edge but reintroduces duplicate sends under any
                      at-least-once scheduler or retry, with the entire customer base
                      as blast radius — the table is load-bearing, not ceremony.
Next action:          add the unique constraint in the same migration as the table
Verification:         Not run — deltas are design estimates, not measured from a graph
```

**E — Enforcement**

```text
Scope:           new digest subsystem
Stack:           Other — unknown
Input:           three Enforcement handoffs from A, one from L
Decision:        Defer (encoding) — rules stated in encoding-neutral form
Config files:    unknown until the stack is known; then per the JS or Python sibling skill
Subsystems:      digest-core, digest-job, digest-store, digest-facade (+ catch-all last)
Forbidden edges: digest-core -> *  except_to digest-core   (pure core)
                 * -> digest-internal-*  except digest-*   (facade only)
                 * -> <provider SDK>  except <email adapter> (one email mechanism)
                 digest-* -> <usage internals>  except the usage inbound interface
Reject rule:     "at most one email per owner per week" is behavior, not an edge →
                 coverage check via the unique constraint and a test (defect-shift-left)
Verification:    Not run — no linter, no stack
Next action:     identify the stack, then write the rule file in the same PR as the code,
                 rules first (§6)
```

Residual risk:      deliverability and spam placement; whether the content is useful
Manual evaluation:  one send to an internal account before the first real run
Handoffs:           shift-left (placement), observability (residual), traceability (engagement)

**H — Shift left**

| Defect class | Earliest stage (rank) | Mechanism | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Duplicate send | 0 | unique `(account_id, period_start)` — makes it unrepresentable | Proceed |
| Opted-out owner included | 0 → 6 | one recipient query as the only path; unit test | Proceed |
| Forbidden digest import | 2 (else 5) | the E rules in editor + CI | Proceed |
| Unsubscribe authorization gap | 1 (else 7) | decide the signed-token model in design; negative tests | Proceed |
| Wrong figures in pure core | 6 | unit test, fixed fixtures | Proceed |
| Broken/empty template render | 6 | snapshot of `render` | Proceed |
| New-table migration vs live schema | 8a | migration dry-run | Proceed |
| Missing provider key in target env | 8a | secret-presence check | Proceed |
| Job not scheduled in target env | 8a | config-vs-env check on the schedule entry | Proceed |
| Staging sends to real customers | 8a | sandbox key + recipient allowlist asserted pre-deploy | **Gap today** |

Detection Gap: non-prod leakage to real customers is catchable at Stage 8a (rank 8) but, with no such check, first surfaces at Stage 10 (rank 11) — as mail to a real customer. Mechanism: assert at boot and pre-deploy that a non-prod environment holds a sandbox provider key and a recipient allowlist. Build it with the slice.

**Observability**

```text
Subject:           weekly-digest production signals
Residual risk:     the weekly run silently stops — owners simply stop receiving mail
Duty:              Detect
Signal:            metric — sends completed per run, and eligible owners per run
Measured at:       the digest_send table, i.e. what the recipient population actually got
Threshold:         zero sends in a run where eligible > 0
Actor:             the on-call owner of the digest subsystem
First action:      trigger the run manually — it is idempotent, so a re-run is safe
Time to detect:    ≤24h vs tolerable <7 days (must be caught before the next run)
Decision:          ADD
Review interval:   quarterly
Next action:       ship the counter and this one alert with the job, not after

Residual risk:     provider rejects a share of sends
Signal:            metric — failed ÷ eligible per run
Decision:          DEMOTE — dashboard panel, not a page; it has no distinct first
                   action beyond the zero-sends alert
Review interval:   quarterly

Residual risk:     the email is delivered, opened, and useless
Decision:          UNOBSERVED by this skill — open and click rate is outcome evidence
                   for digest-engagement and belongs to requirements-traceability,
                   not to failure detection. Consequence if left unwired: the
                   BUILD-minimal revisit trigger cannot fire, and the feature
                   survives on sentiment.
Next action:       instrument open/click in the same PR so the 4-send window can close
```
